ESV.1: The word of the LORD came to me:
ESV.2: “Son of man, propound a riddle, and speak a parable to the house of Israel;
ESV.3: say, Thus says the Lord GOD: A great eagle with great wings and long pinions, rich in plumage of many colors, came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar.
ESV.4: He broke off the topmost of its young twigs and carried it to a land of trade and set it in a city of merchants.
ESV.5: Then he took of the seed of the land and planted it in fertile soil.  He placed it beside abundant waters. He set it like a willow twig,
ESV.6: and it sprouted and became a low spreading vine, and its branches turned toward him, and its roots remained where it stood. So it became a vine and produced branches and put out boughs.
ESV.7: “And there was another great eagle with great wings and much plumage, and behold, this vine bent its roots toward him and shot forth its branches toward him from the bed where it was planted, that he might water it.
ESV.8: It had been planted on good soil by abundant waters, that it might produce branches and bear fruit and become a noble vine.
ESV.9: “Say, Thus says the Lord GOD: Will it thrive? Will he not pull up its roots and cut off its fruit, so that it withers, so that all its fresh sprouting leaves wither? It will not take a strong arm or many people to pull it from its roots.
ESV.10: Behold, it is planted; will it thrive? Will it not utterly wither when the east wind strikes it — wither away on the bed where it sprouted?”
ESV.11: Then the word of the LORD came to me:
ESV.12: “Say now to the rebellious house, Do you not know what these things mean? Tell them, behold, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, and took her king and her princes and brought them to him to Babylon.
ESV.13: And he took one of the royal offspring  and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath (the chief men of the land he had taken away),
ESV.14: that the kingdom might be humble and not lift itself up, and keep his covenant that it might stand.
ESV.15: But he rebelled against him by sending his ambassadors to Egypt, that they might give him horses and a large army. Will he thrive? Can one escape who does such things? Can he break the covenant and yet escape?
ESV.16: “As I live, declares the Lord GOD, surely in the place where the king dwells who made him king, whose oath he despised, and whose covenant with him he broke, in Babylon he shall die.
ESV.17: Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company will not help him in war, when mounds are cast up and siege walls built to cut off many lives.
ESV.18: He despised the oath in breaking the covenant, and behold, he gave his hand and did all these things; he shall not escape.
ESV.19: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: As I live, surely it is my oath that he despised, and my covenant that he broke. I will return it upon his head.
ESV.20: I will spread my net over him, and he shall be taken in my snare, and I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there for the treachery he has committed against me.
ESV.21: And all the pick  of his troops shall fall by the sword, and the survivors shall be scattered to every wind, and you shall know that I am the LORD; I have spoken.”
ESV.22: Thus says the Lord GOD: “I myself will take a sprig from the lofty top of the cedar and will set it out. I will break off from the topmost of its young twigs a tender one, and I myself will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
ESV.23: On the mountain height of Israel will I plant it, that it may bear branches and produce fruit and become a noble cedar. And under it will dwell every kind of bird; in the shade of its branches birds of every sort will nest.
ESV.24: And all the trees of the field shall know that I am the LORD; I bring low the high tree, and make high the low tree, dry up the green tree, and make the dry tree flourish. I am the LORD; I have spoken, and I will do it.”

NKJV.1: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
NKJV.2: “Son of man, pose a riddle, and speak a parable to the house of Israel,
NKJV.3: and say, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD:  “A great eagle with large wings and long pinions, Full of feathers of various colors, Came to Lebanon And took from the cedar the highest branch.
NKJV.4: He cropped off its topmost young twig And carried it to a land of trade; He set it in a city of merchants.
NKJV.5: Then he took some of the seed of the land And planted it in a fertile field; He placed it by abundant waters And set it like a willow tree.
NKJV.6: And it grew and became a spreading vine of low stature; Its branches turned toward him, But its roots were under it. So it became a vine, Brought forth branches, And put forth shoots.
NKJV.7: “But there was another great eagle with large wings and many feathers; And behold, this vine bent its roots toward him, And stretched its branches toward him, From the garden terrace where it had been planted, That he might water it.
NKJV.8: It was planted in good soil by many waters, To bring forth branches, bear fruit, And become a majestic vine.” ’
NKJV.9: “Say, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: “Will it thrive?  Will he not pull up its roots, Cut off its fruit, And leave it to wither? All of its spring leaves will wither, And no great power or many people Will be needed to pluck it up by its roots.
NKJV.10: Behold, it is planted, Will it thrive? Will it not utterly wither when the east wind touches it? It will wither in the garden terrace where it grew.” ’ ”
NKJV.11: Moreover the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
NKJV.12: “Say now to the rebellious house: ‘Do you not know what these things mean?’ Tell them, ‘Indeed the king of Babylon went to Jerusalem and took its king and princes, and led them with him to Babylon.
NKJV.13: And he took the king’s offspring, made a covenant with him, and put him under oath. He also took away the mighty of the land,
NKJV.14: that the kingdom might be brought low and not lift itself up, but that by keeping his covenant it might stand.
NKJV.15: But he rebelled against him by sending his ambassadors to Egypt, that they might give him horses and many people. Will he prosper? Will he who does such things escape? Can he break a covenant and still be delivered?
NKJV.16: ‘As I live,’ says the Lord GOD, ‘surely in the place where the king dwells who made him king, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke—with him in the midst of Babylon he shall die.
NKJV.17: Nor will Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company do anything in the war, when they heap up a siege mound and build a wall to cut off many persons.
NKJV.18: Since he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, and in fact gave his hand and still did all these things, he shall not escape.’ ”
NKJV.19: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: “As I live, surely My oath which he despised, and My covenant which he broke, I will recompense on his own head.
NKJV.20: I will spread My net over him, and he shall be taken in My snare. I will bring him to Babylon and try him there for the treason which he committed against Me.
NKJV.21: All his fugitives with all his troops shall fall by the sword, and those who remain shall be scattered to every wind; and you shall know that I, the LORD, have spoken.”
NKJV.22: Thus says the Lord GOD: “I will take also one of the highest branches of the high cedar and set it out. I will crop off from the topmost of its young twigs a tender one, and will plant it on a high and prominent mountain.
NKJV.23: On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it; and it will bring forth boughs, and bear fruit, and be a majestic cedar. Under it will dwell birds of every sort; in the shadow of its branches they will dwell.
NKJV.24: And all the trees of the field shall know that I, the LORD, have brought down the high tree and exalted the low tree, dried up the green tree and made the dry tree flourish; I, the LORD, have spoken and have done it.”

NASB.1: Now the word of the LORD came to me saying,
NASB.2: 'Son of man, propound a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel,
NASB.3: saying, 'Thus says the Lord GOD, 'A great eagle with great wings, long pinions and a full plumage of many colors came to Lebanon and took away the top of the cedar.
NASB.4: 'He plucked off the topmost of its young twigs and brought it to a land of merchants; he set it in a city of traders.
NASB.5: 'He also took some of the seed of the land and planted it in fertile soil. He placed [it] beside abundant waters; he set it [like] a willow.
NASB.6: 'Then it sprouted and became a low, spreading vine with its branches turned toward him, but its roots remained under it. So it became a vine and yielded shoots and sent out branches.
NASB.7: 'But there was another great eagle with great wings and much plumage; and behold, this vine bent its roots toward him and sent out its branches toward him from the beds where it was planted, that he might water it.
NASB.8: 'It was planted in good soil beside abundant waters, that it might yield branches and bear fruit [and] become a splendid vine.''
NASB.9: 'Say, 'Thus says the Lord GOD, 'Will it thrive? Will he not pull up its roots and cut off its fruit, so that it withers-- so that all its sprouting leaves wither? And neither by great strength nor by many people can it be raised from its roots [again].
NASB.10: 'Behold, though it is planted, will it thrive? Will it not completely wither as soon as the east wind strikes it-- wither on the beds where it grew?'''
NASB.11: Moreover, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
NASB.12: 'Say now to the rebellious house, 'Do you not know what these things [mean]?' Say, 'Behold, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took its king and princes and brought them to him in Babylon.
NASB.13: 'He took one of the royal family and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath. He also took away the mighty of the land,
NASB.14: that the kingdom might be in subjection, not exalting itself, [but] keeping his covenant that it might continue.
NASB.15: 'But he rebelled against him by sending his envoys to Egypt that they might give him horses and many troops. Will he succeed? Will he who does such things escape? Can he indeed break the covenant and escape?
NASB.16: 'As I live,' declares the Lord GOD, 'Surely in the country of the king who put him on the throne, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, in Babylon he shall die.
NASB.17: 'Pharaoh with [his] mighty army and great company will not help him in the war, when they cast up ramps and build siege walls to cut off many lives.
NASB.18: 'Now he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, and behold, he pledged his allegiance, yet did all these things; he shall not escape.''
NASB.19: Therefore, thus says the Lord GOD, 'As I live, surely My oath which he despised and My covenant which he broke, I will inflict on his head.
NASB.20: 'I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My snare. Then I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there [regarding] the unfaithful act which he has committed against Me.
NASB.21: 'All the choice men in all his troops will fall by the sword, and the survivors will be scattered to every wind; and you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.'
NASB.22: Thus says the Lord GOD, 'I will also take [a sprig] from the lofty top of the cedar and set [it] out; I will pluck from the topmost of its young twigs a tender one and I will plant [it] on a high and lofty mountain.
NASB.23: 'On the high mountain of Israel I will plant it, that it may bring forth boughs and bear fruit and become a stately cedar. And birds of every kind will nest under it; they will nest in the shade of its branches.
NASB.24: 'All the trees of the field will know that I am the LORD; I bring down the high tree, exalt the low tree, dry up the green tree and make the dry tree flourish. I am the LORD; I have spoken, and I will perform [it].'

CSB17.1: The word of the LORD came to me:
CSB17.2: “Son of man, pose a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.3: You are to say, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says: A huge eagle with powerful wings, <sup>ⓓ</sup> long feathers, and full plumage of many colors came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.4: He plucked off its topmost shoot, brought it to the land of merchants, and set it in a city of traders.
CSB17.5: Then he took some of the land’s seed and put it in a fertile field; <sup>ⓕ</sup> he set it like a willow, <sup>ⓖ</sup> a plant <sup>[1]</sup> by abundant water.
CSB17.6: It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height with its branches turned toward him, <sup>ⓗ</sup> yet its roots stayed under it. So it became a vine, produced branches, and sent out shoots.
CSB17.7: “‘But there was another huge eagle with powerful wings and thick plumage. And this vine bent its roots toward him! It stretched out its branches to him from the plot where it was planted, <sup>ⓘ</sup> so that he might water it.
CSB17.8: It had been planted in a good field by abundant water in order to produce branches, bear fruit, and become a splendid vine.’
CSB17.9: “You are to say, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says: Will it flourish? Will he not tear out its roots <sup>ⓙ</sup> and strip off its fruit so that it shrivels? All its fresh leaves will wither! Great strength and many people will not be needed to pull it from its roots.
CSB17.10: Even though it is planted, will it flourish? Won’t it wither completely when the east wind strikes it? <sup>ⓚ</sup> It will wither on the plot where it sprouted.’”
CSB17.11: The word of the LORD came to me:
CSB17.12: “Now say to that rebellious house, <sup>ⓛ</sup> ‘Don’t you know what these things mean? ’ Tell them, ‘The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took its king and officials, <sup>ⓜ</sup> and brought them back with him to Babylon.
CSB17.13: He took one of the royal family <sup>ⓝ</sup> and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath. <sup>ⓐ</sup> Then he took away the leading men of the land,
CSB17.14: so that the kingdom would be humble and not exalt itself <sup>ⓑ</sup> but would keep his covenant in order to endure.
CSB17.15: However, this king revolted against him <sup>ⓒ</sup> by sending his ambassadors to Egypt so they might give him horses and a large army. <sup>ⓓ</sup> Will he flourish? Will the one who does such things escape? Can he break a covenant and still escape?
CSB17.16: “‘As I live — this is the declaration of the Lord GOD  — he will die in Babylon, in the land of the king who put him on the throne, <sup>ⓔ</sup> whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke.
CSB17.17: Pharaoh with his mighty army and vast company will not help him in battle, <sup>ⓕ</sup> when ramps are built and siege walls constructed to destroy many lives.
CSB17.18: He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. He did all these things even though he gave his hand in pledge. <sup>ⓖ</sup> He will not escape!
CSB17.19: “‘Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: As I live, I will bring down on his head my oath that he despised and my covenant that he broke.
CSB17.20: I will spread my net over him, <sup>ⓗ</sup> and he will be caught in my snare. <sup>ⓘ</sup> I will bring him to Babylon and execute judgment on him there for the treachery he committed against me. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.21: All the fugitives <sup>[2]</sup> among his troops will fall by the sword, and those who survive will be scattered to every direction of the wind. <sup>ⓚ</sup> Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.

AMP.1: Now the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
AMP.2: "Son of man, ask a riddle and tell a parable to the house of Israel,
AMP.3: saying, 'Thus says the Lord GOD, "A great eagle (Nebuchadnezzar) with great wings, long pinions and a rich plumage of many colors came to Lebanon (Jerusalem) and took away the top of the cedar (Judah).
AMP.4: He broke off the topmost of its young twigs (young King Jehoiachin) and carried it to a land of traders (Babylonia); he set it in a city of merchants (Babylon).
AMP.5: He also took some of the seed of the land ( Zedekiah, of the royal family) and planted it in fertile soil and a fruitful field; he placed it beside abundant waters and set it like a willow tree.
AMP.6: Then it sprouted and grew and became a low, spreading vine whose branches turned [in submission] toward him, but its roots remained under it. So it became a vine and yielded shoots and sent out branches.
AMP.7: "There was [also] another great eagle with great wings and many feathers; and behold, this vine (Zedekiah) bent its roots toward him and sent out its branches toward him, away from the beds where it was planted, for him to water.
AMP.8: It was planted in good soil where water was plentiful for it to produce leaves and branches and to bear fruit, so that it might become a splendid vine."'
AMP.9: Thus says the Lord GOD, 'Ask, "Will it thrive? Will he (Nebuchadnezzar) not uproot it and strip off its fruit so that all its sprouting leaves will wither? It will not take a strong arm or many people to uproot it [ending Israel's national existence].
AMP.10: Though it is planted, will it thrive and grow? Will it not completely wither when the east wind touches it? It will wither in the beds where it grew."'"
AMP.11: Moreover, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
AMP.12: "Say now to the rebellious house, 'Do you not know (realize) what these things mean?' Tell them, 'Hear this, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and took its king [Jehoiachin] and its princes and brought them with him to Babylon.
AMP.13: And he took a member of the royal family [the king's uncle, Zedekiah] and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath. He also took the important leaders of the land,
AMP.14: so that the kingdom would be in subjection, unable to restore itself and rise again, but that by keeping his covenant it might continue.
AMP.15: But Zedekiah rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar by sending his ambassadors to Egypt so that they might give him horses and many troops. Will he succeed? Will he who does such things escape? Can he indeed break the covenant [with Babylon] and [still] escape?
AMP.16: As I live,' says the Lord GOD, 'surely in the country of the king (Nebuchadnezzar) who made Zedekiah [the vassal] king, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, in Babylon Zedekiah shall die.
AMP.17: Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company will not help him in the war, when they (the Babylonians) put up ramps and build siege walls to destroy many lives.
AMP.18: Now Zedekiah dishonored the oath by breaking the covenant, and behold, he gave his hand and pledged his allegiance, yet did all these things; he shall not escape.'"
AMP.19: Therefore, thus says the Lord GOD, "As I live, I will bring down on his own head My oath [made on My behalf by Nebuchadnezzar] which Zedekiah dishonored and My covenant which he broke.
AMP.20: I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My snare; and I will bring him to Babylon and will enter into judgment with him there for his treason which he has committed against Me.
AMP.21: All the choice men [from Judah] in all his troops will fall by the sword, and those that survive will be scattered to every wind; and you will know [without any doubt] that I the LORD have spoken."
AMP.22: Thus says the Lord GOD, "I Myself will take a twig from the lofty top of the cedar and will set it out; I will crop off from the topmost of its young twigs a tender one and I will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
AMP.23: I will plant it on the mountain heights of Israel, that it may grow boughs and bear fruit and be a noble and stately cedar. And birds of every kind will live under it; they will nest [securely] in the shade of its branches.
AMP.24: All the trees of the field will know that I the LORD bring down the tall tree, exalt the low tree, dry up the green tree, and make the dry tree flourish. I am the LORD; I have spoken, and I will fulfill it."
